title: Extraction and Analysis of Pollen from Fossil Insects
author: Grímsson, Ulrich, et al.
materials: Agar Low Viscosity Resin Embedding Kit

steps.title: Prepare Toluidine blue stain
steps.instruction: Mix 50 mg Toluidine blue (0.05 % w/v) with distilled water to a final volume of 100 mL in a beaker; stir with a magnetic stirrer. Store the solution at 4 °C; it remains usable for up to one year.

steps.title: Prepare potassium permanganate stain
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g potassium permanganate (1 % w/v) in distilled water to a final volume of 100 mL in a beaker; stir. Store the solution at 4 °C; it can be kept indefinitely.

steps.title: Set up microscope for pollen detection
steps.instruction: Place the fossil specimen under a stereomicroscope (dissecting microscope) and adjust magnification and focus so the whole insect or the desired part (leg, abdomen, head, etc.) is clearly visible. Timing may range from minutes to hours; extracting a single pollen grain takes about 5 min.

steps.title: Locate exoskeletal pollen with fluorescence
steps.instruction: Turn on epi‑fluorescence illumination; pollen grains adhering to the exoskeleton will illuminate under the fluorescence beam.

steps.title: Prepare glycerine drop on slide
steps.instruction: Place a small drop of glycerine in the centre of a light‑microscope slide, label the slide appropriately, and keep the slide close at hand.

steps.title: Extract exoskeletal pollen (dry specimen)
steps.instruction: Using a teasing needle or a micromanipulator equipped with a nasal hair, dip the tip into the glycerine drop, then gently touch the dry pollen grain. If the grain is stuck, first loosen it with the teasing needle and then pick it up with the wet micromanipulator tip; push the grain along the surface so it adheres to the hair.

substeps.instruction: Loosen pollen with teasing needle if needed.
Push wet hair along surface to capture pollen.

steps.title: Extract exoskeletal pollen (wet specimen)
steps.instruction: For specimens already preserved in glycerine, quickly blot most of the surface glycerine with a paper napkin (allow absorption without scraping), then use a teasing needle and/or micromanipulator to pick up the pollen.

substeps.instruction: Blot excess glycerine with paper napkin, avoiding scraping.
Extract pollen with teasing needle or micromanipulator.

steps.title: Transfer pollen to glycerine slide
steps.instruction: Dip the micromanipulator tip (with the attached pollen) into the prepared glycerine drop on the slide; the pollen will automatically detach from the hair and remain suspended in the drop.

steps.title: Locate internal pollen in abdomen
steps.instruction: Observe the fossil under the stereomicroscope; note whether the abdomen is flat or protruding and look for yellow or orange masses that indicate pollen preserved inside the digestive system.

steps.title: Prepare glycerine drop for internal pollen
steps.instruction: Place another small drop of glycerine on a LM microscope slide and keep it nearby.

steps.title: Extract gut pollen
steps.instruction: Using a fine teasing needle, puncture the abdomen and gently scrape out part of the gut content that contains pollen.

steps.title: Transfer gut pollen to slide
steps.instruction: Deposit the scraped gut content into the glycerine drop on the LM slide; dipping the micromanipulator tip releases the pollen into the drop.
